newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli mutual funds post net inflow in January.
newsitem.headline: Israeli mutual funds post net inflow in January.

text.p: Israeli mutual funds enjoyed a net inflow of money in January for the first time in three years, Meitav Investments and Securities said on Wednesday.

Israel's 310 mutual funds had a net inflow of approximately 141 million shekels in January. Combined with an average return of 7.1 percent, total assets for the funds grew 8.2 percent to 14.66 billion shekels at the end of January, Meitav said in its monthly report.

Nearly all the inflow, 128 million shekels, was in share funds. Bond funds continued to experience net redemptions totalling about 45 million shekels, said Meitav, a brokerage house and fund manager that tracks the mutual fund industry.
The inflow comes as the stock market enters the third month of a rally. In January alone the General Share index rose 14.7 percent, Meitav noted.
"The positive trend was expressed not only in rising share prices but in increased turnover," said Meitav.

The mutual funds suffered redemptions of about 20 billion shekels in 1994-96 during which the Israeli share market was in a slump and the public soured on the stock market. In 1996 alone, fund assets fell 15.8 percent, Meitav said, as net redemptions reached 4.1 billion shekels.
Many analysts see the mutual funds as a barometer of small-investor interest in the stock market. But Meitav warned that the change in trend during January did not signal a turnaround in sentiment
It noted that most of the inflow was into the more speculative Caram funds that invest in small-capitalisation stocks.

"It seems therefore that the purchases of mutual fund units were by those already in the market and there is still no sign yet that the next circle investors, the 'broad public', is joining in," Meitav said.
